items.title: Send these readings to your care team this week
items.text: 6.3% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL (weeks 11-12); the usual target is under 5%. Your average was 176.9 mg/dL. Contact your care team this week rather than waiting for your next visit.

rejected.text: Your average blood sugar was 176.9 mg/dL, and you should contact your care team this week. They can help you understand your readings, which were above 250 mg/dL 6.3% of the time.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal may be linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with a walk after dinner linked to a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller. Walking 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain, with a rise 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You didn't have any scored dinners that started at 8 pm or later, which is good because sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Keep having dinner before 8 pm to avoid a bigger rise in sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 14.5 hours of overnight fasting, with 100.0% of nights reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone in the program.
